title: A Shark That Walks? Meet the Ocean's Newest Waddling Wonder!
summary: Have you ever seen a shark walk? Not swim—walk! Divers off Papua New Guinea just found a brand-new shark that does exactly that. It's called the Dudgeon's walking shark, and it uses its fins to wiggle across shallow reefs. Picture a small, spotted shark scooting over rocks in water barely up to your knees. That's how it hunts for snacks! The discovery was a total surprise. Scientist Christine Dudgeon was looking for a different walking shark—one with leopard spots. But when her team pulled up this little guy, it had brown dots and white dashes instead. "I was so excited!" she said. They checked nearby reefs and found 11 more in just two days. All had the same pattern. Bingo—a new species! Walking sharks aren't like the huge ones in movies. They're small and live in shallow coral reefs. Their special "walk" helps them when the tide goes out and leaves puddles of water with low oxygen. While other fish might struggle, these sharks just stroll around to find food. Scientists think this skill evolved so they could survive in tricky reef flats. So far, this new shark has only been spotted in three places. That means it could be in danger if its home gets damaged by pollution or climate change. But the good news? There are probably more surprises hiding in shallow seas. As Dudgeon says, sharks "continue to surprise and fascinate us." Who knows what will walk—or swim—out of the ocean next?
why_it_matters: This discovery shows that there are still amazing animals hiding in the ocean, and protecting nature helps keep surprises like walking sharks safe for you to learn about and maybe see one day.

background_read: Papua New Guinea (a country in the Pacific Ocean north of Australia) has some of the richest coral reefs on Earth.
Walking sharks are a small group of sharks found only around Australia and New Guinea. Scientists didn’t know they existed until a few decades ago.
New species are still being discovered in shallow tropical seas, which shows how much of the ocean remains a mystery.

WHAT: Discovered a brand-new walking shark with brown dots and white dashes
WHERE: Shallow reefs off the coast of Papua New Guinea
WHY: The team was searching for a different walking shark but found this one instead

perspectives.description: They are thrilled because a new species means there is so much more to learn about life in the sea. Every discovery adds a piece to the puzzle of how animals survive.

perspectives.perspective: Conservationists Worried About the Shark’s Home
perspectives.description: They point out that this shark lives only in a few small reef areas. Pollution or rising ocean temperatures could easily destroy that home and make the shark disappear forever.
They see this as proof that the planet still has secrets waiting to be found—maybe even something no one has ever seen before, right under the shallow water.
